ops.title: hermes → Apple container: live prototype verdict (2026-07-15) — sandbox PROVEN (w/ a required proxy fix), lifecycle is the remaining blocker
ops.body:
# hermes-on-Apple-container — live-prototype verdict (2026-07-15)

Supersedes the 2026-07-14 spike memo (note 452679f). Executes the 5-experiment matrix from backlog task 89dbaae on the live host (apple/container 1.1.0 + socktainer 1.1.1 installed with user approval). Full chronology + artifacts: cc-notes log `apple-container-prototype` (carries the verified proxy-fix diff as an attachment).

**Verdict: still NO-GO for immediate production, but the blockers narrowed sharply. The prototype turned "unknown, prototype-able" into "sandbox proven (with one small, verified proxy fix); memory/backup/egress favorable-to-neutral; the SINGLE remaining architectural blocker is lifecycle/recovery (#158/#286 — no boot-autostart, no restart policy)."** That blocker is upstream-tracked and buildable-around, not fundamental.

## Conjunctive gate table

| Gate | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Sandbox path** | ✅ **CONDITIONAL PASS** | proxy→socktainer→apiserver→micro-VM: all 14 allowlisted routes work; 9 host-escape create-bodies 403'd. **BUT** the codex refuter found a CRITICAL host-escape (below); it is **fixed + verified**. Holds only WITH the fix. |
| **Egress isolation** | ✅ **PASS by default** | Crown-jewel host `:8000` AND the entire fleet (192.168.64.x) are unreachable from a container with ZERO pf rules (cross-vmnet isolation + no host-loopback exposure). Only the default network's NAT internet is open; custom nets are fully isolated. |
| **Recovery / lifecycle** | ❌ **FAIL as-is / achievable-with-work** | NO component auto-restarts (apiserver #158; socktainer + proxy unsupervised) — the standing blocker. Recovery needs a KeepAlive supervision layer (the fleet's `write_agent` pattern already exists). Cold-boot leg deferred (no-reboot constraint). |
| **Memory** | ✅ **PARTIAL PASS** | ~340 MB RSS per idle micro-VM (our measurement; the unsourced ~200 MB was low). A 2G machine holds only ~356 MB idle — NO pre-wiring, favorable vs tart's full 4 GiB. No-release-shrink + 24h growth: deferred (measurement contamination + time). |
| **Backup** | ✅ **PASS** | Bind-mount host paths keep the current restic file-level model (files appear directly on host). Named volumes are opaque ext4 images → migration MUST bind-mount hermes state, never named volumes. |
| *(bonus)* **Wholesale NixOS-in-a-machine** | ⚠️ **boot-blocked** | Not gate-critical (sandbox gate met by the socktainer path). Apple machine rootfs is read-only; NixOS's `/etc/resolv.conf` symlink into `/nix/store` fails Apple's `configureDns`. A scoped image-fix (writable `/etc` overlay) was attempted; needs real image engineering. |

## The critical finding (why the adversarial pass mattered)
socktainer transparently relays a container-internal `/var/run/docker.sock` **target** to its own raw, unfiltered API — regardless of mount source. hermes-docker-proxy screens bind/mount **sources** but never **destinations**. Exploit run end-to-end THROUGH the proxy: `docker run -v <bindroot>/empty:/var/run/docker.sock` (passes screening) → inside, that path is a live socktainer socket → `docker run --privileged -v /:/hostroot` mounted the **HOST filesystem** (read `/Users/yasyf` = sops key + vault token). Full proxy bypass → host compromise. **Fixed**: a `forbiddenDest()` destination screen (blocks any mount whose target basename is `docker.sock`) — verified to 403 the exploit (both `-v` and `--mount`), leave legit binds working, and keep existing tests green. Diff attached to the log; backlog task da1c63 to port it. (Not currently exploitable on the live dockerd proxy — dockerd has no such relay — but a hard socktainer-migration prerequisite and cheap defense-in-depth now.)

## Production prerequisites the migration must satisfy (conjunctive)
1. **Proxy destination-screening** (task da1c63) — REQUIRED; ready fix verified.
2. **Lifecycle supervision** — a KeepAlive/boot-autostart wrapper for apiserver + socktainer + proxy + the agent machine (mirrors the tart `write_agent` stack). The one architectural build item; upstream #158/#286 would obviate it.
3. **tailscale in-container** — userspace-networking mode (proven to start; no caps needed); the agent reaches metal over the tailnet since the fleet is unreachable via vmnet. Full join+reach-metal test pending an ephemeral tag:hermes key.
4. **Bind-mount state** (not named volumes) so restic keeps working.
5. **Drop `--runtime runsc`** from the agent's docker args (socktainer ignores it; the per-VM boundary replaces gVisor — a STRONGER boundary).
6. Optional: the wholesale-NixOS-machine path if the "keep systemd+dockerd+proxy intact" route is preferred over rebuilding hermes as OCI containers — needs the read-only-rootfs image work.

## What's proven vs still open
PROVEN: sandbox filtering (with fix), egress isolation by default, per-VM memory footprint, restic-compatible bind-mount backup, tailscale userspace mechanism, subnet-collision avoidance (192.168.72/24 override).
OPEN (deferred, not blocking the verdict): 24h memory soak + no-release quantification; cold-boot recovery (no-reboot constraint); full tailnet join (user authkey); pf internet-egress enforcement (root-gated, largely redundant given default isolation); the wholesale-NixOS boot; the create-body field audit (VM-isolated, low risk).

## Re-evaluation triggers (standing watch — task ad1beb, log has the one-command check)
apple/container #158 (boot autostart) or #286 (restart policy) closing removes the lifecycle blocker → strong GO signal. Also: #66 Docker-API reversal, a first-party egress primitive, ballooning completion, new container/socktainer releases.
